notes.title: Buybacks do not tell the whole story
notes.markdown:
**Synthesis:** compare recurring buyback demand with recurring supply becoming available over the same period. Revenue-funded purchases can shrink during weak markets while scheduled releases continue. But unlocks are not necessarily sales, and buybacks are not mathematically doomed.

- **Issuance** creates tokens; **unlocks** make existing tokens transferable; **buybacks** purchase tokens; **burns** destroy them. A treasury buyback does not automatically remove supply permanently.
- Hypothetical illustration, September 5: buying 5 tokens while 10 unlock gives 0.5× gross coverage. It does not forecast price or imply all 10 will sell.
- App revenue, validator income, tokenholder returns and token price are different outcomes. **Correction:** Solana still burns 50% of base fees; prioritization fees go to validators. “Solana has no fee burn” is inaccurate. [Official fee rules, checked September 5](https://solana.com/docs/core/fees)

**Say it aloud:** “A buyback is one source of demand. I still need to know new available supply, who sells, and where the purchased tokens go.”

Deeper: [[Token Buybacks and Emissions]] · [[Value Capture]].

notes.title: CLARITY: procedure versus law
notes.markdown:
- Its core subject is the legal framework for digital commodities and SEC/CFTC responsibilities. **Synthesis:** clearer statutory rules can make long-term planning less dependent on changing agency interpretations; passage would not automatically approve every token or business model. [Congressional summary of the introduced bill](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633)
- Staff statements and statutes have different legal weight. The SEC’s liquid-staking statement explicitly says it has no legal force and covers specified circumstances. [SEC statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corpfin-certain-liquid-staking-activities-080525)
- **Dated procedural check:** the Senate Press Gallery’s September 4 notice says the H.R. 3633 cloture motion ripens September 15, 2026, at 2:15 p.m. That is not a record of enactment. [Senate notice](https://www.dailypress.senate.gov/friday-september-4-2026/)

**Say it aloud:** “CLARITY matters for durable market rules; a procedural vote is not the same as a bill becoming law.”

Deeper: [[Policy and Regulation]]; the older note’s vote predictions and product-specific legal conclusions were not comprehensively rechecked.

notes.title: What decentralization measures miss
notes.markdown:
- A validator is a participant; its **client is the software** implementing the shared rules. Agave and Jito-Solana share a lineage; full Firedancer is independently implemented, while Frankendancer combines Firedancer components with Agave. Independent code reduces shared-bug risk. [Agave](https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave), [Jito-Solana](https://github.com/jito-foundation/jito-solana), [Firedancer](https://github.com/firedancer-io/firedancer)
- **Nakamoto coefficient:** for the Solana voting metric discussed, count the smallest set of largest validators reaching roughly one-third of voting power—enough to obstruct finalization, not automatically steal funds or rewrite valid history. [Historical metric definition](https://solana.com/uk/news/network-health-report-june-2025)
- **19 was supplied in the study discussion, not verified as today’s value.** It suggests meaningful distribution, with no universal “good” cutoff. Compare consistent definitions, trends, operator independence, software, geography and shared hosting. [Hosting concentration criteria](https://solana.org/delegation-criteria)

**Say it aloud:** “The coefficient counts how many validators can block progress; it does not tell me how independent those validators really are.”

Deeper: [[Validator Clients]] · [[Network Reliability and Concentration]].

notes.title: Alpenglow, in a few sentences
notes.markdown:
- **Mechanism:** Votor replaces TowerBFT voting with direct validator messages and quorum certificates; Rotor is a later block-propagation upgrade. In the design checked September 5, the fast path uses at least 80% stake in one round; the fallback uses 60% thresholds over two rounds. [Solana upgrade description](https://solana.com/upgrades/alpenglow)
- **Latency:** Anza’s approximately 150 ms median is a simulation-based finality estimate excluding computation overhead, not a measured end-to-end payment guarantee. Submission, inclusion, execution, RPC and application delays also matter. [Anza](https://www.anza.xyz/blog/alpenglow-a-new-consensus-for-solana)
- **Guarantee:** `confirmed` means a supermajority voted; `finalized` is the network’s strongest commitment state. Faster finality shortens the wait before acting on that stronger state. It does not eliminate software, custody or application risk. [RPC commitment definitions](https://solana.com/docs/rpc#configuring-state-commitment)

**Say it aloud:** “Alpenglow aims to make strong settlement confirmation fast enough to wait for; finality time and total user waiting time are different measurements.”

Deeper: [[Alpenglow]] · [[Finality — Optimistic vs Deterministic]] · [[Slot Times and Latency]].

notes.title: Institutional adoption: the recall sheet
notes.markdown:
### Bank settlement and conversion

| Who | Confirmed scope | Date and source |
|---|---|---|
| Visa · Cross River Bank · Lead Bank | These banks started settling Visa obligations in USDC on Solana, with seven-day settlement; consumer card checkout is unchanged. Select participants, within Visa's multichain strategy. | [Dec. 16, 2025 — Visa](https://corporate.visa.com/en/sites/visa-perspectives/newsroom/visa-launches-stablecoin-settlement-in-the-united-states.html) |
| Singapore Gulf Bank | Launched bank-account mint/redeem service for corporate and high-net-worth customers; Solana among supported chains. USDC transactions above $100,000 at launch; fee waiver was promotional. | [Apr. 17, 2026 — SGB](https://www.sgb.com/insights/singapore-gulf-bank-launches-stablecoin-mint-and-redeem-service) |

### Remittances and cash access

| Who | Confirmed scope | Date and source |
|---|---|---|
| Western Union · Anchorage Digital Bank | USDPT launched on Solana, issued by Anchorage; agent treasury and consumer services were still developing. Token launch does not mean the whole remittance network migrated. | [May 4, 2026 — Western Union](https://ir.westernunion.com/news/archived-press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Western-Union-Launches-USDPT-on-Solana-Advancing-Regulated-Digital-Infrastructure-for-Global-Payments/default.aspx) |
| MoneyGram | Ramps launched for Solana apps: cash-in in 25+ countries, cash-out in 170+ countries/territories; Rift identified as the first integrated wallet. Footprint measures availability, not usage. | [Aug. 11, 2026 — launch report](https://solana.com/news/moneygram-ramps) |

### Capital markets and tokenized funds

| Who | Confirmed scope | Date and source |
|---|---|---|
| J.P. Morgan · Galaxy | Arranged a commercial-paper issuance on public Solana with delivery-versus-payment; Coinbase and Franklin Templeton purchased it, with proceeds in USDC. One securities transaction, not bankwide adoption. | [Dec. 11, 2025 — J.P. Morgan](https://www.jpmorgan.com/about-us/corporate-news/2025/jpmorgan-commercial-paper-issuance-solana-blockchain) |
| WisdomTree | Extended its regulated tokenized fund suite to Solana, including money-market, equity and fixed-income products, as part of a multichain strategy. | [Jan. 28, 2026 — WisdomTree](https://ir.wisdomtree.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/774/wisdomtree-expands-tokenization-ecosystem-to-solana) |
| Coinbase Asset Management · Superstate | CUSHY share class added to Solana; qualified-purchaser restrictions apply. DeFi integrations are described as coming soon; tokenization does not imply instant redemption. | [July 2026 — roundup](https://solana.com/news/solana-ecosystem-roundup-july-2026); [current fund page checked Sept. 5](https://superstate.com/assets/cushy) |

**Say it aloud:** “Look for live settlement, bank conversion and cash access, then ask about repeat usage and volume.” This is our analytical framework, not a proven ranking. Deeper: [[Institutional Rails and RWAs]] · [[Payments on Solana]] · [[Tokenized Equities]].
